column1: # Global scrub rules for share-skill — Peter's unambiguous personal identifiers.
# Format: <find><TAB><replace>   (literal strings, no regex). Blank lines and
# lines starting with '#' are ignored. Applied to every skill on publish by
# publish-skill.sh, BEFORE the per-skill .scrub file.
# ONLY put ALWAYS-private, unambiguous tokens here — things that are never a
# false positive: home-directory paths, personal emails, phone numbers,
# calendar IDs. Do NOT add names ("Peter Hartree" must survive for README
# attribution), cities, client names, or project names — those are
# context-dependent and belong in each skill's own .scrub file.
# Personal email addresses
your-email@gmail.com
your-email@example.com
your-product@gmail.com
your-email@example.com
your-email@example.com
# Calendar IDs
your-meetings-calendar-id@group.calendar.google.com
# Phone numbers
# Home-directory paths (leak the OS username "ph"). Trailing slash on purpose:
# it avoids false positives like "/Users/phil/" while covering the common case
# where the path has a further component ("~/foo" -> "~/foo"). It does
# NOT catch a bare "/Users/ph" with no trailing slash (rare in skill content);
# the per-skill review is the backstop for that.
